name: push-tag-human-approved-correction
body:
Decision record for the C1+C2 amendment to `agent-builder-roster-cleanup` (the second-amendment correction of the release-agent amendment).

SOURCE. The coordinator's amendment brief: (C1) the recurring law is "push/tag remain human-**approved** acts", not "human acts" — correct the phrasing on every agent-policy and binary-doc surface; (C2) only the optional `release-agent` is ever granted `git push`/`git tag`, and its grant is `ask` (not `allow`); every other generated agent gets no push/tag grant at all (denied by deny-by-default); the navigator still captures explicit user consent before dispatching the release-agent. Two earlier amendment attempts were cancelled before landing, so none of their edits exist.

INCONSISTENCY. The first amendment's live nodes described the release-agent's push/tag grant as `allow` (autonomous once invoked) and left every other generated agent on `ask`; the law's name was "human acts". The agent-builder template therefore instructed scaffolding push/tag `ask` on every generated agent. All of that contradicts the corrected model.

RESOLUTION [with coordinator]. New requirement `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only` (feature `agent-builder-roster-cleanup`, under `requirements.stakeholder.agent-suite-maintainer`) covers C1+C2; it drives the reused `domain.entity.release-agent-flow`, whose body was corrected (`allow` → `ask`, "human acts" → "human-approved acts", ordinary generated agents denied). The law nodes were amended in place: `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out`, `requirements.constraint.agent-changes-always-on-main`, `solution.constraint.agent-builder-roster-truthful`, and the requirement bodies `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent` and `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-main-flow` (phrasing), plus the component body `solution.component.agent-builder-prompt` and the prior note `requirements.note.release-agent-amendment-decision` (both had stale `allow`/`human acts` wording).

SPINE. requirement ⊃ `requirements.stakeholder.agent-suite-maintainer`; `drives` → `domain.entity.release-agent-flow`; that entity is `realised-by` the three reused agent-policy components (`agent-builder-prompt`, `codebase-navigator-prompt`, `agent-roster-docs`) plus the NEW narrow `solution.component.push-tag-policy-surfaces` (its `implemented-by` set: `Cargo.toml`, `src/git/mod.rs`, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs`, `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.plan_verify_at`, `tests/git_e2e.rs`, `tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`); `contains` that component under `solution.container.scanner-cli`.

COMPONENTS REUSED vs CREATED. Reused (as the brief directs): `solution.component.agent-builder-prompt` → `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`; `solution.component.codebase-navigator-prompt` → `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`; `solution.component.agent-roster-docs` → `AGENTS.md` + `README.md`. Created: `solution.component.push-tag-policy-surfaces`, `implemented-by` exactly the binary-doc/test surfaces this change-set edits (`Cargo.toml`, `src/git/mod.rs`, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs`, `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.plan_verify_at`, `tests/git_e2e.rs`, `tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`) — no existing component anchors those FQNs without also spanning an untouched file (see the component body).

JUDGEMENT CALLS.
1. `plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md` line 71 says "push/tag remain human acts"; per the brief it is a historical plan record and is left untouched — only noted here.
2. FOLLOW-UP FOLD-IN [with coordinator]. A later amendment fold brought the two surfaces the first pass knew of but left out into scope: `README.md:411` ("Push/tag remain human.") is now named in `solution.component.agent-roster-docs`'s body (README.md is already its `implemented-by`, so no new edge was needed), and the `apg plan verify` merge-handoff string at `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs:200` (inside the real function `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.plan_verify_at`) is now named in the requirement's C1 surface list and attached to `solution.component.push-tag-policy-surfaces` with a new `implemented-by` edge. No test asserts that string (verified), so it is a clean `modifies` target. Because the component's `implemented-by` set changed, the verify gate's derived coverage (`rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.coverage_check`) now also enforces `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.plan_verify_at`. `.opencode/agents/implementation-phase-reviewer.md` remains a consumer artifact regenerated out-of-band and is NOT edited.
3. The reuse of `agent-roster-docs` is safe for coverage: its `implemented-by` set (AGENTS.md + README.md) is already reached by the earlier amendment, and README.md is edited by the sibling requirement, so no fake task is forced (the same honest-coverage reasoning recorded in `solution.note.agent-roster-narrow-owners`).
